content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble fully understanding the memory address areas in the latest [product_name] [version_no]. From what I've gathered, the VRV section keeps the values entered even after a power cycle. For example, if I put 100 into VRW0 and reboot the controller, it starts up with 100 in VRW0. The VW section only keeps its value if the parameter is mapped in a function block; for example, using V1 in a mathematical instruction mapped to V0, enter 100 into VW0, and after a power cycle, it is retained in VW0. However, I'm not sure about the VXW section—is its behavior like VW? Additionally, I've noticed that when using SD cards with the web server, the controller seems to start with the value stored in the function block's program and copied to the SD card during download. Changing VW0 to 110 with an SD card inserted results in the controller starting with 100 again on the next power up. Does anyone have information or documentation explaining these memory areas in more detail?

You're not alone in finding the new V memory areas confusing. I haven't found any [company_name] document that provides a clear explanation. Even after contacting support, the answers I received were unsatisfactory, and I couldn't find any helpful application examples. This topic has come up in multiple forums, but so far all explanations seem speculative.

It's reassuring to know that I'm not the only one struggling with this. The behavior of the memory addresses gets even more confusing when an SD card is inserted. Currently, I'm experimenting with [product_name] [version_no] without an SD card, and VW, VX, and VR seem to act similarly after a power cycle (except VW and VX only retain values when stored in the parameter VM mapping). I'll share my results after I test with an SD card as well.
Just an idea—have you tried checking documentation in Chinese?

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are experiencing confusion and frustration because documentation regarding the behavior of VRW, VW, and VXW memory areas in the latest [product_name] [version_no] is unclear, especially concerning value retention after power cycling and the impact of using SD cards. The official support and manuals seem inadequate, forcing users to rely on trial and error.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear, easily accessible, and official documentation explaining how memory areas work, including details about their behavior with or without SD cards and after a power cycle.
